title: Columbus lands on Hispaniola
description: Christopher Columbus reached the island of Hispaniola, beginning European contact with the territory that would become Haiti.

title: France gains western Hispaniola
description: Under the Treaty of Ryswick, Spain ceded the western third of Hispaniola to France, creating the colony of Saint-Domingue.

title: Haitian Revolution begins
description: Enslaved Africans launched a massive uprising against French rule, igniting the only successful large-scale slave revolt in history.

title: Haiti declares independence
description: Haiti proclaimed independence from France, becoming the first independent Black republic and the first nation born of a slave revolt.

title: France imposes independence indemnity
description: France recognized Haiti's independence only in exchange for a crippling indemnity payment, burdening the new nation with decades of debt.

title: United States occupation begins
description: U.S. Marines landed in Haiti, beginning a military occupation that would last nearly two decades.

title: End of U.S. occupation
description: American forces withdrew, restoring Haitian sovereignty after nineteen years of occupation.

title: Catastrophic earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck near Port-au-Prince, killing over 200,000 people and devastating the capital.

title: Copán dynasty founded
description: K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' founded the Maya dynasty at Copán, which became a major center of Classic Maya art and science.

title: Columbus reaches Honduras
description: On his fourth voyage, Columbus reached the Caribbean coast of Honduras, the first European to do so.

title: Spanish conquest begins
description: Spanish forces under Cristóbal de Olid and others began the conquest and colonization of Honduras.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Honduras declared independence from Spain alongside the other Central American provinces.

title: Honduras becomes a sovereign republic
description: Honduras seceded from the United Provinces of Central America to become a fully independent republic.

title: Hurricane Mitch devastates Honduras
description: One of the deadliest Atlantic hurricanes killed thousands and destroyed much of the country's infrastructure.

title: Coup ousts President Zelaya
description: President Manuel Zelaya was removed from office and expelled from the country in a coup d'état, triggering a political crisis.

title: Columbus arrives in Jamaica
description: Christopher Columbus landed on Jamaica during his second voyage, claiming the island for Spain.

title: England seizes Jamaica from Spain
description: English forces captured Jamaica, beginning more than three centuries of British colonial rule.

title: Port Royal earthquake
description: A devastating earthquake and tsunami sank much of Port Royal, then one of the busiest ports in the Caribbean.

title: Abolition of slavery
description: Britain abolished slavery across its empire, beginning emancipation for Jamaica's enslaved population.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Jamaica gained full independence from the United Kingdom, becoming a sovereign nation within the Commonwealth.

title: Bob Marley and reggae's global rise
description: The death of Bob Marley marked the global ascent of Jamaican reggae, one of the island's most influential cultural exports.

title: Usain Bolt's Olympic triumph
description: Sprinter Usain Bolt won triple gold at the Beijing Olympics, setting world records and elevating Jamaica's sporting prestige.

title: Olmec civilization flourishes
description: The Olmec, considered the mother culture of Mesoamerica, built early cities such as San Lorenzo and carved colossal stone heads.

title: Rise of Teotihuacan
description: Teotihuacan grew into one of the largest cities of the ancient world, home to the great Pyramids of the Sun and Moon.

title: Founding of Tenochtitlan
description: The Mexica (Aztecs) founded Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco, the future capital of a powerful empire.

title: Fall of the Aztec Empire
description: Spanish forces led by Hernán Cortés, with Indigenous allies, conquered Tenochtitlan, ending the Aztec Empire.

title: War of Independence begins
description: Father Miguel Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores launched Mexico's war of independence against Spanish colonial rule.

title: Independence from Spain achieved
description: Mexico secured its independence from Spain, ending three centuries of colonial rule.

title: Mexican Revolution begins
description: A decade-long revolution erupted against the Díaz dictatorship, reshaping Mexican society, land rights, and government.

title: NAFTA takes effect
description: The North American Free Trade Agreement opened Mexico's economy to free trade with the United States and Canada.

title: Columbus reaches the coast
description: Christopher Columbus sailed along the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua during his fourth voyage.

title: Spanish found Granada and León
description: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba established the cities of Granada and León, among the oldest colonial cities in the Americas.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Nicaragua declared independence from Spain as part of the broader Central American emancipation.

title: Defeat of William Walker
description: Central American forces defeated American filibuster William Walker, who had seized power and declared himself president of Nicaragua.

title: United States occupation
description: U.S. Marines occupied Nicaragua to protect American interests, beginning years of intervention in the country's affairs.

title: Sandinista Revolution
description: The Sandinista National Liberation Front overthrew the Somoza dictatorship, ending decades of dynastic rule.

title: Democratic election ends civil war
description: Violeta Chamorro won the presidency in free elections, helping bring the Contra war to a close.

title: Balboa reaches the Pacific
description: Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama and became the first European to sight the Pacific Ocean from the Americas.

title: Founding of Panama City
description: The Spanish founded Panama City, which became a key hub for trade and the transport of treasure across the isthmus.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Panama declared independence from Spain and voluntarily joined Simón Bolívar's Gran Colombia.

title: Independence from Colombia
description: Panama separated from Colombia with U.S. support, paving the way for construction of the interoceanic canal.

title: Panama Canal opens
description: The Panama Canal opened, linking the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and transforming global maritime trade.

title: U.S. invasion ousts Noriega
description: The United States invaded Panama and removed military leader Manuel Noriega from power.

title: Canal handed over to Panama
description: The United States transferred full control of the Panama Canal to Panama under the Torrijos-Carter Treaties.

title: Columbus sights the islands
description: Christopher Columbus sighted the islands of Saint Kitts and Nevis during his second voyage.

title: First English Caribbean colony
description: English settlers established Saint Kitts as the first English colony in the Caribbean, a base for further expansion.

title: Treaty of Paris confirms British rule
description: The Treaty of Paris ended Anglo-French rivalry over the islands, securing them firmly under British control.

title: Abolition of slavery
description: Slavery was abolished across the British Empire, beginning emancipation on the sugar plantations of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

title: Associated statehood with Britain
description: Saint Kitts and Nevis gained internal self-government as an associated state of the United Kingdom.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Saint Kitts and Nevis became fully independent, the youngest sovereign nation in the Americas.

title: Early English settlement attempt
description: Shipwrecked English colonists made an early attempt to settle Saint Lucia but were driven off by the Indigenous Kalinago.

title: French establish a colony
description: The French established a lasting settlement on Saint Lucia, beginning long colonial rivalry with Britain over the island.

title: Britain gains permanent control
description: The Treaty of Paris confirmed British possession of Saint Lucia after the island had changed hands many times.

title: Abolition of slavery
description: Britain's abolition of slavery began emancipation for the enslaved people of Saint Lucia.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Saint Lucia gained full independence from the United Kingdom, remaining within the Commonwealth.

title: Derek Walcott wins Nobel Prize
description: Saint Lucian poet Derek Walcott was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, a landmark for Caribbean culture.

title: Columbus sights Saint Vincent
description: Christopher Columbus is said to have sighted Saint Vincent during his third voyage to the Americas.

title: Island ceded to Britain
description: The Treaty of Paris ceded Saint Vincent to Britain, intensifying European settlement and conflict with the Indigenous people.

title: Second Carib War
description: The Garifuna (Black Caribs) fought British forces; their defeat led to the deportation of thousands from the island.

title: Abolition of slavery
description: Slavery was abolished across the British Empire, beginning emancipation in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines became an independent nation within the Commonwealth.

title: La Soufrière volcano erupts
description: The La Soufrière volcano erupted explosively, forcing the evacuation of thousands of residents from the north of the island.

title: Columbus reaches Trinidad
description: Christopher Columbus arrived at Trinidad during his third voyage, naming the island for the Holy Trinity.

title: Britain captures Trinidad
description: British forces captured Trinidad from Spain, later adding Tobago to form a single colony.

title: Abolition of slavery
description: Britain abolished slavery, beginning emancipation for the enslaved Africans on Trinidad's plantations.

title: Indian indentured laborers arrive
description: The first ship of indentured workers from India arrived, profoundly shaping Trinidad's population and culture.

title: Invention of the steelpan
description: The steelpan, the only acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century, emerged from Trinidad's working-class communities.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Trinidad and Tobago gained independence from the United Kingdom, becoming a sovereign nation.

title: Trinidad and Tobago becomes a republic
description: The nation adopted a republican constitution, replacing the British monarch with a president as head of state.

title: Founding of Jamestown
description: English settlers established Jamestown in Virginia, the first permanent English colony in North America.

title: Declaration of Independence
description: The thirteen American colonies declared independence from Great Britain, founding the United States.

title: U.S. Constitution drafted
description: Delegates drafted the Constitution, establishing the framework of the federal government still in use today.

title: Civil War begins
description: The American Civil War erupted between the Union and the Confederacy, largely over slavery and states' rights.

title: Emancipation Proclamation
description: President Lincoln declared enslaved people in Confederate states to be free, a turning point toward abolition.

title: Women win the right to vote
description: The Nineteenth Amendment was ratified, guaranteeing American women the constitutional right to vote.

title: Civil Rights Act
description: Landmark legislation outlawed discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.

title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
description: NASA's Apollo 11 mission landed the first humans on the Moon, a milestone in science and exploration.
